edits.purpose: B3: render the complement-truth explanation (was only in the never-taken branch) and scope the structural argument
edits.new:
On this design the complement's true effect is **exactly 0**: the DGM sets
$b(W) = \beta_2$ on $\{W \le 30\}$ and $0$ elsewhere
(`guohe_sec52_truth.R:75`), and the family starts at $30$, so every
$\hat H^c = \{W > \hat c\}$ lies inside the null region and complement
coverage is simply upper $\ge 0$. The structural argument above concerns this
design's nested family, in which $\hat H^c$ is never a candidate. It is not
claimed for Guo and He's two-subgroup design (their Section 5.1), where the
complement of the selected subgroup is the other candidate — with two
candidates, the argmin — nor for their MONET1 families (their Section 4), which
contain each subgroup and its complement.

edits.purpose: B5 callout: identification has one dimension here; the null cell as reference; overshoot reaches the estimand
edits.old:
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Classification is not the right lens on this design, and its arithmetic says
why.** The true harm region is $H = \{W \le 30\}$ and every candidate is
$S(c) = \{W \le c\}$ with $\hat c \ge 30$, so $H = S(30) \subseteq S(\hat c)$
for every replicate. With $W \sim \mathrm{Unif}(0, 80)$ the classification
operating characteristics are therefore closed forms in $\hat c$ alone:

- **Sensitivity $\equiv 1$** and **NPV $\equiv 1$** — *identically*, by nesting,
  not by merit. Both are degenerate by construction on this design, so neither
  is tabulated: a column of ones would read as a result when it is an artefact
  of $H \subseteq S(\hat c)$.
- **Specificity** $= (80 - \hat c)/50$ — reported per cell above.
- **PPV** $= 30/\hat c$ — reported per cell above.

Sensitivity carries no information in this design. The whole of the
identification story is how far $\hat c$ overshoots $30$, which the $\hat c$
distribution above reports directly and which specificity and PPV then restate
as monotone functions of it.
:::
edits.new:
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**On this design identification has one dimension, and its arithmetic says
why.** The true harm region is $H = \{W \le 30\}$ and every candidate is
$S(c) = \{W \le c\}$ with $\hat c \ge 30$, so $H = S(30) \subseteq S(\hat c)$
for every replicate. With $W \sim \mathrm{Unif}(0, 80)$ the classification
operating characteristics are therefore closed forms in $\hat c$ alone:

- **Sensitivity $\equiv 1$** and **NPV $\equiv 1$** (for $\beta_2 > 0$) —
  *identically*, by nesting, not by merit. Both are degenerate by construction
  on this design, so neither is tabulated: a column of ones would read as a
  result when it is an artefact of $H \subseteq S(\hat c)$.
- **Specificity** $= (80 - \hat c)/50$ — reported per cell above.
- **PPV** $= 30/\hat c$ — reported per cell above.

The whole of the identification story is how far $\hat c$ overshoots $30$,
which the $\hat c$ distribution above reports directly and which specificity
and PPV then restate as monotone functions of it. Two further readings follow
from the same arithmetic. At $\beta_2 = 0$ there is no harm region: every
selection is a false identification, specificity and PPV are not defined as
accuracy there, and that cell's $\hat c$ distribution is the reference for the
argmax's own pull toward the smallest candidate, $c = 30$ — where the true
boundary of the other cells sits. And overshoot reaches the estimand:
$\gamma_{\hat c} = \beta(\hat c)$ is a weighted average of $b(\cdot)$ over
$[0, \hat c]$ (Guo and He, Section 5.2), so it falls below $\beta_2$ as
$\hat c$ overshoots, which the mean $\gamma_{\hat c}$ column shows.
:::

edits.purpose: B6: limit 1 re-grounded on this design's records; E1 ranges and dev/notes read removed; limit 3 acknowledges G&H Section 6; limit 5 added; cert-note chunk removed

```{r b6}
#| output: asis
# The field's coverage figures are COMPUTED from the rendered bundles, never
# transcribed, so this paragraph cannot go stale against the tables above.
# Rewritten 2026-09-11 (dev/tasks/claude_cc_task_guohe_record_payload_2026-09-11.md):
# limit 1 is grounded on this design's own records (its earlier regime
# attribution came from campaign e1stud, not from this design); the E1 range
# citations and the dev/notes read are removed; limit 3 acknowledges Guo & He
# Section 6.
fld_cov   <- SUM$cover[SUM$method == "MR (field)"]
fld_bias  <- SUM$bias[SUM$method == "MR (field)"]
fld_lo3   <- sort(fld_cov)[1:3]
fld_min   <- sprintf("%.3f", min(fld_lo3))
fld_range <- sprintf("%.3f–%.3f", min(fld_lo3), max(fld_lo3))
fld_bias_range <- sprintf("%+.3f to %+.3f", min(fld_bias), max(fld_bias))
stopifnot(all(fld_bias > 0))  # limit 1 states the bias is positive in every cell
phat_med   <- vapply(CELLS, function(id) median(bun[[id]]$results$p_hat_H), numeric(1))
phat_range <- sprintf("%.3f–%.3f", min(phat_med), max(phat_med))
.cu <- vapply(CMP, function(b) mean(b$results$c_cover_95_s), numeric(1))
stopifnot(BETA2[which.min(.cu)] == 0)  # limit 1 places the complement's low point at the null cell
cmp_low <- sprintf("%.3f", min(.cu))

cat(sprintf(paste0(
"Five limits belong on the record, stated plainly.\n\n",

"1. **The field's low points are under-correction on a nested family.** ",
"Across these cells the MR (field) one-sided coverage **bottoms out at %s**, ",
"with the three lowest cells spanning %s, and its point estimate est2 keeps a ",
"positive bias in every cell (%s). The committed 16-cell record reads the ",
"nested family as the hardest case for the second-order correction, ",
"consistent with the first proof-of-concept's reading that the excess is a ",
"property of unequal candidate variances under nesting ",
"(`REPORT_mr_field_vs_guohe_2026-09-05.md:34`). The complement bound's low ",
"point, %s, is the null cell, where the selection is loosest ",
"(`REPORT_mr_complement_vs_guohe_2026-09-09.md:174`), and re-selection is ",
"spread thin throughout (median $\\hat p(\\hat H)$ %s; B5): these shortfalls ",
"sit where the pick is least settled. The design is also Guo and He's own ",
"ground. It illustrates their continuum results (their Section 3, Theorems ",
"4–5), whereas its ~151 candidates, each differing from its neighbour by one ",
"subject, are the near-duplicate case that strains the no-tie condition (A5) ",
"behind our construction's theory (supplement Section S5, \"No-tie ",
"regularity\"). The field's calibration here is an empirical finding on this ",
"design, not a consequence of that theory.\n\n",

"2. **The complement and joint figures in @sec-b3 belong to this design ",
"alone.** They say nothing about forestsearch's own screened identifier, ",
"which is evaluated separately (campaign `e1stud`, ",
"`REVIEW_E1_fields_2026-09-08.md`, whose pre-registered complement criterion ",
"was not met, `:10`).\n\n",

"3. **Guo & He is not run on forestsearch's screened family.** Their method ",
"is applied exactly as published, on the family their Section 5.2 specifies. ",
"Guo and He suggest (their Section 6) that when identification involves other ",
"considerations their bound serves as a conservative approach; that ",
"suggestion is not tested here, and no claim is made either way.\n\n",

"4. **Everything here is one-sided.** Every construction compared in this ",
"section is one-sided, so none of it depends on the choice of two-sided ",
"interval method.\n\n",

"5. **Identification is flattered by construction.** The true boundary is ",
"the family's smallest member, toward which the argmax is drawn even at ",
"$\\beta_2 = 0$; ",
"sensitivity and NPV are identically 1 for $\\beta_2 > 0$, and overshoot is ",
"the only identification error (B5). The screen and forestsearch's family ",
"construction are not exercised, the complement's truth is 0 in every cell ",
"(so a benefit claim is never tested), and everything is at $n = 400$.\n"),
fld_min, fld_range, fld_bias_range, cmp_low, phat_range))
```

edits.new:
# Manuscript payload

The manuscript section is drafted from this payload, not from the tables above.
It is a superset, so trimming the section never forces a rebuild, and every
element is computed here from the committed bundles: nothing is re-run and
nothing is typed. Bounds are on the oriented log-hazard-ratio scale; each `_hr`
column is $\exp$ of the corresponding mean log-scale bound.

```{r export-payload}
#| output: asis
# TASK dev/tasks/claude_cc_task_guohe_record_payload_2026-09-11.md.
# Location pattern transplanted from the export-payload chunk of
# quarto/applications/actg175/analysis_actg175_continuous_oc.qmd:
# <qmd dir>/_payloads/<stem>/<stem>_payload.rds.
.qmd_dir  <- tryCatch(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)),
                      error = function(e) getwd())
.qmd_stem <- tryCatch(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(knitr::current_input())),
                      error = function(e) "guohe_supp_section")
.out_dir  <- file.path(.qmd_dir, "_payloads", .qmd_stem)
dir.create(.out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
.payload_file <- file.path(.out_dir, paste0(.qmd_stem, "_payload.rds"))

# (1) The bound for gamma_c-hat on t7: SUM (B2, unchanged) plus the mean bound.
.low <- do.call(rbind, lapply(CELLS, function(id) data.frame(
  cell = id, method = METHODS,
  mean_lower = vapply(METHODS, function(m)
    mean(method_cols(bun[[id]]$results, m, REPRO[[id]], FIXR[[id]])$low),
    numeric(1)),
  row.names = NULL)))
bound_t7 <- merge(SUM, .low, by = c("cell", "method"), sort = FALSE)
bound_t7 <- bound_t7[order(match(bound_t7$cell, CELLS),
                           match(bound_t7$method, METHODS)), ]
bound_t7$beta2 <- BETA2[match(bound_t7$cell, CELLS)]
bound_t7$mean_lower_hr <- exp(bound_t7$mean_lower)
rownames(bound_t7) <- NULL

# (2) Identification on t7 (H = {W <= 30}; no harm region at beta2 = 0).
ident_t7 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(CELLS), function(k) {
  r <- bun[[CELLS[k]]]$results; ch <- r$c_hat
  data.frame(cell = CELLS[k], beta2 = BETA2[k],
    chat_min = min(ch), chat_q25 = unname(quantile(ch, 0.25)),
    chat_med = median(ch), chat_q75 = unname(quantile(ch, 0.75)),
    chat_max = max(ch), p_chat_30 = mean(abs(ch - 30) < 1e-9),
    spec_mean = if (BETA2[k] == 0) NA_real_ else mean((80 - ch) / 50),
    ppv_mean  = if (BETA2[k] == 0) NA_real_ else mean(30 / ch),
    n_sel_mean = mean(r$n_sel), n_sel_med = median(r$n_sel),
    gamma_mean = mean(r$theta), dilution = BETA2[k] - mean(r$theta),
    phat_med = median(r$p_hat_H), phat_q25 = unname(quantile(r$p_hat_H, 0.25)),
    phat_q75 = unname(quantile(r$p_hat_H, 0.75)), phat_mean = mean(r$p_hat_H),
    M_eff_med = median(r$M_eff),
    sd_marg = sd(r$fld_est2), sd_err = sd(r$fld_est2 - r$theta),
    row.names = NULL)
}))

# (3) Complement and joint on t7 (complement truth exactly 0: cover = upper >= 0).
#     naive = cgate_naive_est + z95 * cgate_se_wald, the engine's own naive
#     convention (se_wald = the candidate SE; R/fs_mr_inference.R naive block);
#     IJ two-term = cgate_est + z95 * cgate_se_ij, mirroring the harm side's
#     lower_1s. Definitions are quoted in the Stage 0 record.
.up_row <- function(u, n) { x <- sum(u >= 0); w <- wilson(x, n)
  c(cover = x / n, lo = unname(w["lo"]), hi = unname(w["hi"])) }
comp_t7 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(CELLS), function(k) {
  r <- CMP[[CELLS[k]]]$results; n <- nrow(r)
  up <- list(naive   = r$cgate_naive_est + z95 * r$cgate_se_wald,
             ij      = r$cgate_est + z95 * r$cgate_se_ij,
             field   = r$c_upper_95,
             field_s = r$c_upper_95_s)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(up), function(m) {
    cv <- .up_row(up[[m]], n)
    data.frame(cell = CELLS[k], beta2 = BETA2[k], method = m,
      cover = cv[["cover"]], cover_lo = cv[["lo"]], cover_hi = cv[["hi"]],
      mean_upper = mean(up[[m]]), mean_upper_hr = exp(mean(up[[m]])),
      row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))
joint_t7 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(CELLS), function(k) {
  r <- CMP[[CELLS[k]]]$results; n <- nrow(r)
  ws <- wilson(sum(r$joint_cover_s), n); wu <- wilson(sum(r$joint_cover), n)
  data.frame(cell = CELLS[k], beta2 = BETA2[k],
    joint_s = mean(r$joint_cover_s), joint_s_lo = unname(ws["lo"]),
    joint_s_hi = unname(ws["hi"]),
    joint = mean(r$joint_cover), joint_lo = unname(wu["lo"]),
    joint_hi = unname(wu["hi"]),
    corr_mean = mean(r$joint_corr), corr_s_mean = mean(r$joint_corr_s),
    pair_lower_H = mean(r$h_lower_975),
    pair_lower_H_hr = exp(mean(r$h_lower_975)),
    pair_upper_Hc_s = mean(r$c_upper_975_s),
    pair_upper_Hc_s_hr = exp(mean(r$c_upper_975_s)),
    row.names = NULL)
}))

# (3b) The naive convention on the harm side: the section's naive row is the
#      replication's (Cox SE); the complement's naive row uses the engine's SE.
#      Both conventions on the harm side, so the difference is on record.
naive_convention <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(CELLS), function(k) {
  r <- bun[[CELLS[k]]]$results
  data.frame(cell = CELLS[k], beta2 = BETA2[k],
    cover_replication_se = mean(r$naive_cover),
    cover_engine_se = mean(r$naive_est - z95 * r$mr_se_wald <= r$theta),
    mean_se_replication = mean(r$naive_se), mean_se_engine = mean(r$mr_se_wald),
    row.names = NULL)
}))

# (4) The committed 16-cell paired record, harm side only, at r = 1/12 and 1/30.
#     Column reads transplanted from mr_field_vs_guohe.qmd (method_cols).
P16 <- c(sprintf("t35_beta2_%02d", 0:5), sprintf("t6_k%02d", c(2L, 6L, 10L, 12L)),
         CELLS)
.b16 <- c(lapply(stats::setNames(P16[1:10], P16[1:10]), function(id)
  readRDS(sprintf("mr_field_vs_guohe_%s.rds", id))), bun)
.m16 <- c("Naive", "G&H r=1/12", "G&H r=1/30", "MR (field)", "MR (IJ)")
.c16 <- function(res, meth) switch(meth,
  "Naive"      = list(est = res$naive_est, low = res$naive_lower, cov = res$naive_cover),
  "G&H r=1/12" = list(est = res$gh_r2_deb, low = res$gh_r2_low, cov = res$gh_r2_cov),
  "G&H r=1/30" = list(est = res$gh_r4_deb, low = res$gh_r4_low, cov = res$gh_r4_cov),
  "MR (field)" = list(est = res$fld_est2,  low = res$fld_lower_1s, cov = res$fld_cover_1s),
  "MR (IJ)"    = list(est = res$mr_est,    low = res$mr_lower_1s,  cov = res$mr_cover))
pre16 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(P16, function(id) {
  res <- .b16[[id]]$results
  do.call(rbind, lapply(.m16, function(meth) {
    v <- .c16(res, meth); n <- length(v$est); w <- wilson(sum(v$cov), n)
    data.frame(cell = id, method = meth, cover = mean(v$cov),
      cover_lo = unname(w["lo"]), cover_hi = unname(w["hi"]),
      margin = mean(v$est - v$low), bias = mean(v$est - res$theta), n = n,
      row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))
pre16$design <- ifelse(grepl("^t35", pre16$cell), "Tables 3-5: two complementary subgroups",
                ifelse(grepl("^t6", pre16$cell), "Table 6: k disjoint null subgroups",
                       "Table 7: nested continuum"))

payload <- list(
  bound_t7 = bound_t7, ident_t7 = ident_t7, comp_t7 = comp_t7,
  joint_t7 = joint_t7, naive_convention = naive_convention, pre16 = pre16,
  meta = list(
    nrep = NREP, mcse = MCSE, draws = DRAWS, field_R_out = R_OUT,
    field_R_in = R_IN, r_fixed = "1/12 (G&H r=1/12: r2 / gh_r2 columns)",
    scale = "oriented log-HR; *_hr = exp(mean log-scale bound)",
    complement_truth = 0,
    head_at_render = tryCatch(system("git rev-parse HEAD", intern = TRUE),
                              error = function(e) NA_character_),
    inputs_md5 = tools::md5sum(c(sprintf("mr_field_vs_guohe_%s.rds", P16),
                                 sprintf("guohe_repro_%s.rds", CELLS),
                                 sprintf("mr_field_complement_vs_guohe_%s.rds", CELLS))),
    built_at = Sys.time(), R = R.version.string,
    forestsearch_version = tryCatch(as.character(utils::packageVersion("forestsearch")),
                                    error = function(e) NA_character_)))
saveRDS(payload, .payload_file)

for (nm in c("bound_t7", "ident_t7", "comp_t7", "joint_t7", "naive_convention",
             "pre16")) {
  print(knitr::kable(payload[[nm]], digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
                     caption = sprintf("Payload element `%s`.", nm)))
  cat("\n")
}
cat("Payload written to `", file.path("_payloads", .qmd_stem,
    paste0(.qmd_stem, "_payload.rds")), "`.\n\n", sep = "")
```
